episode_summary: May 2019 MakerDAO interview (part 1) with Nik Kunkel on the crypto-economics of DAI: how ETH-backed loans mint DAI, the MKR token as risk absorber and governance, the stability fee and peg levers, liquidation auctions, and the plans for multi-collateral DAI.

cards.claim: In May 2019 Nik Kunkel said locking ETH to draw DAI leaves the ETH owned by the user, who must repay the loan to get it back.
cards.speaker: Nik Kunkel
cards.quote: the eth is still yours it's just you need to pay back your loan in order to get it back

cards.claim: In May 2019 the host described locking $150 of ETH to mint $100 of DAI, with the ETH as collateral for the loan.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: So if you put $150 worth of F and the smart contract we'll talk about, you're going to mint $100 in DAI as a loan that's collateralized by your Ethereum.

cards.claim: In May 2019 Nik Kunkel said the most common Maker user holds DAI to hedge rather than borrowing against ETH.
cards.speaker: Nik Kunkel
cards.quote: this is actually the most common user we have right they they don't want to take out a loan

cards.claim: In May 2019 Nik Kunkel said the MKR token exists to segregate risk, absorbing the risk and reward that DAI holders avoid.
cards.speaker: Nik Kunkel
cards.quote: it's really a way of segregating risk. So as a DAI user, you don't want to have any risk.

cards.claim: In May 2019 Nik Kunkel said Maker's fees would buy and burn MKR, making MKR deflationary if the system ran well.
cards.speaker: Nik Kunkel
cards.quote: all those fees go towards basically buying up and burning the MKR token. So that makes MKR deflationary if it's run well.

cards.claim: In May 2019 Nik Kunkel explained that underwater debt would be covered by automatically minting and selling new MKR.
cards.speaker: Nik Kunkel
cards.quote: The way they cover that is that the system automatically starts minting new MKR and then selling that MKR until the debt is covered.

cards.claim: In May 2019 Nik Kunkel said multi-collateral DAI would be released later that year, enabling many token types as collateral.
cards.speaker: Nik Kunkel
cards.quote: but in later this year we'll be releasing multi-collateral DAI, which will enable all types of tokens.

cards.claim: In May 2019 Nik Kunkel described Maker's governance as a plutocracy in which voting with money rewards good decisions and punishes bad ones.
cards.speaker: Nik Kunkel
cards.quote: It's a plutocracy and it's you vote with your money and if you make good decisions, you get rewarded.

cards.claim: In May 2019 Nik Kunkel said DAI had traded between about 96 and 98 cents for roughly the prior month.
cards.speaker: Nik Kunkel
cards.quote: We were trading between like 96 or 97 and 98 cents.

cards.claim: In May 2019 Nik Kunkel said Maker's stability fee had risen from half a percent at launch to 19.5 percent.
cards.speaker: Nik Kunkel
cards.quote: when we launched, we had an interest rate of half a percent. Currently, we have an interest rate of 19 and a half percent.

cards.claim: In May 2019 Nik Kunkel said MKR holders held a public governance meeting every week to decide whether to raise or lower the interest rate.
cards.speaker: Nik Kunkel
cards.quote: every week we have a public governance type of meeting where all of the MKR holders kind of meet and discuss

cards.claim: In May 2019 Nik Kunkel said the debt ceiling for ETH collateral was 100 million DAI, with about 80 to 81 million DAI in supply.
cards.speaker: Nik Kunkel
cards.quote: Currently for Ethereum, the debt ceiling is 100 million die. So right now the die supply is at around 80 million, 81 million.

cards.claim: In May 2019 Nik Kunkel said liquidated collateral was sold at 3 percent below the oracle price.
cards.speaker: Nik Kunkel
cards.quote: So what we do when a position gets margin call is we sell it at 3% below the price that the oracles are reporting.

cards.claim: In May 2019 Nik Kunkel named Uniswap, Kyber, Radar Relay and DDEX as venues where liquidation arbitrage bots compared prices.
cards.speaker: Nik Kunkel
cards.quote: they'll look at Uniswap, they'll look at Kyber, they'll look at ETH to DAI, they'll look at Radar Relay, they'll look at DDEX

cards.claim: In May 2019 Nik Kunkel said oracle-based liquidation was about to be deprecated in favour of on-chain auctions in the next Maker version.
cards.speaker: Nik Kunkel
cards.quote: this mechanism of liquidating um of liquidating these loans is about to be deprecated in our next version

cards.claim: In May 2019 Nik Kunkel said Maker's collateral auctions could run for a maximum of 24 hours and could end after an hour without a bid.
cards.speaker: Nik Kunkel
cards.quote: So, for example, an auction could run for 24 hours, maximum duration.

cards.claim: In May 2019 Nik Kunkel said Maker's simulations predicted about 80 to 85 percent of auction participants would bid immediately.
cards.speaker: Nik Kunkel
cards.quote: the simulations that we've done show that people are going to come in around like 80, 85% immediately with the first bid

cards.claim: In May 2019 Nik Kunkel said Maker enables marketplaces but does not host them, so it is not itself a decentralized exchange.
cards.speaker: Nik Kunkel
cards.quote: I think we're definitely enabling marketplaces, which I think is amazing, but we're not hosting the marketplace

cards.claim: In May 2019 Nik Kunkel said tokenized assets such as an Amazon stock would make markets global rather than localized.
cards.speaker: Nik Kunkel
cards.quote: instead of having kind of localized markets, we have globalized markets, right?

cards.claim: In May 2019 Nik Kunkel said the largest on-chain MKR vote so far had 185,000 MKR participating.
cards.speaker: Nik Kunkel
cards.quote: the maximum we've gotten thus far has been out of the total 1 billion maker, we got 185,000 MKR to vote

cards.claim: In May 2019 the speakers predicted a rise of stablecoins or better stablecoins in the coming year, with a battle for market share.
cards.speaker: unknown
cards.quote: this year maybe the last of the last part of last year is definitely like a rise of stable coins or better stable coins

cards.claim: In May 2019 the host predicted Maker's stability fee would still rise later that year, possibly to around 28 percent.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: the rate's still going to go up later this year but how high will it go

cards.claim: In May 2019 the host said DAI could bridge PayPal and the crypto world if its price could be modelled reliably.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: it's basically a bridge between PayPal and the crypto world

cards.claim: In May 2019 the host said Maker would be amazing and would eventually work out.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: I think it's going to be amazing, especially when it works out, which it eventually will.

title: MakerDAO pt. 1 - Nik Kunkel
